title: Axiomatic quantum field theory in curved spacetime
locator: Abstract; Sec. 5, eq. (63) (definition of the background with opposite time orientation), eq. (64) and its outline proof, Theorem 3 (PCT theorem) with diagrams (83)-(84), remarks (1)-(2), eqs. (87)-(90), footnote 13
assumptions: Their axioms for operator product coefficients: locality and covariance, microlocal spectrum condition, associativity, asymptotic positivity, analytic and smooth dependence on the metric, among others. Even dimension treated explicitly.
conclusion: Authors' theorem: an antilinear *-isomorphism from the algebra on (M,g,e,T) to the algebra on (M,g,e,-T), commuting with embeddings, with a dual map on state spaces. Authors' gloss: the theorem relates two background structures; in Minkowski spacetime it reduces to the usual theorem by composing with the reflection isometry; in a Robertson-Walker spacetime it relates an expanding universe to the contracting one and nothing within one universe.
proof_status: Stated as a theorem with proof by the authors. Not verified here.
dependencies: Hollands 2004 for eq. (64); Streater-Wightman for the flat theorem.
open_questions: Which realistic theories satisfy the axioms; how the theorem acts on restricted classes of states.
relevance: Supplies the reversal in exactly the form Proposition 2 needs: same manifold, metric and orientation, opposite time orientation.
limits: Read through a text extraction: abstract, opening of Sec. 1, Sec. 5 from the statement of the PCT relation to the end of the remarks. Secs. 2-4 (the axioms in detail) and Sec. 6 were only searched, not read. The proof of eq. (64) was not checked.

title: A general PCT theorem for the operator product expansion in curved spacetime
version: arXiv:gr-qc/0212028v1, 6 December 2002; Commun. Math. Phys. 244 (2004) 209-244, as listed on the arXiv page

limits: Abstract page only, through a summarising fetch. The body was not read.

title: The CPT Theorem
locator: Sec. 1; Sec. 4.1 (Classical PT Theorem for Tensors, Example 5); Theorem 1; Sec. 8 opening
assumptions: Formal field theories given by polynomial expressions in field components and derivatives; Minkowski space of dimension at least 3; invariance under the proper orthochronous Lorentz group; tensor fields for the classical theorem.
conclusion: Authors' theorem: every formal field theory invariant under the proper orthochronous group is invariant under the proper group, for a specified extension of the action. Authors' statement: the direct generalisation to spinors fails; the quantum CPT theorem for spinors is obtained differently.
proof_status: Theorems with proofs by the authors. Not verified here.
open_questions: Non-polynomial laws and laws with inequalities are outside the theorem.
relevance: Classical PT theorem for tensor fields: the flat-spacetime reason a polynomial Lorentz-invariant tensor law cannot use a time orientation. Also the failure of the classical theorem for spinors.
limits: Read through a text extraction: Sec. 1, the passage of Sec. 2 on quantum actions and the caveat on spontaneous and anomalous breaking, Sec. 4.1-4.2, the statement of Theorem 1, the opening of Sec. 8. Secs. 5-7, 9-11 and all proofs were not read. Roberts cites the published version as Greaves and Thomas (2014); the journal reference was not checked.

title: CPT violation implies violation of Lorentz invariance
version: arXiv:hep-ph/0201258v3, 3 December 2002; Phys. Rev. Lett. 89 (2002) 231602 as cited by Chaichian et al.
locator: Abstract; paragraphs around eqs. (1)-(4); eqs. (5)-(22) for the unequal-mass model; summary
assumptions: Wightman framework with spectrum condition and in-cone covariance (stated in his note 3); Lorentz invariance defined to include covariance of time-ordered functions.
conclusion: Author's claim: if CPT fails for a Wightman function of an interacting theory, the corresponding time-ordered function is not covariant. CPT invariance is necessary and not sufficient for Lorentz invariance in his sense. Unequal particle and antiparticle masses give a nonlocal theory.
proof_status: A short argument, disputed by the two records below.
open_questions: Whether the argument applies to any constructed interacting theory.
relevance: Source of the claim that CPT failure needs Lorentz failure; states Jost's theorem.
limits: Read whole in a degraded text extraction; formulas partly illegible.

title: CPT Violation Does Not Lead to Violation of Lorentz Invariance and Vice Versa
version: arXiv:1103.0168v2, 3 April 2011; Phys. Lett. B 699 (2011) 177 as cited by Duetsch and Gracia-Bondia
assumptions: Interaction-picture models with a step function of the time difference times a step function of the squared interval.
conclusion: Authors' claims: the models are invariant under the proper orthochronous group, break T and CPT, and violate microcausality; noncommutative field theories break Lorentz invariance and keep CPT.
open_questions: Whether such nonlocal theories exist as consistent quantum theories.
relevance: Critic of Greenberg: nonlocal, Lorentz-invariant, CPT-violating models whose interaction contains the time order of timelike-separated points.
limits: Read whole in a text extraction. The models are given at the level of an interaction Hamiltonian; no construction of the full theory.

title: On the assertion that PCT violation implies Lorentz non-invariance
locator: Secs. 1, 2 and 5; Theorem 2 in Sec. 4; appendix
assumptions: Causal perturbation theory of Epstein and Glaser for the positive result.
conclusion: Authors' claims: Greenberg's argument presupposes interacting Wightman functions satisfying axioms 0 to II, verified for no realistic model; PCT covariance of time-ordered products can be maintained through causal renormalisation for a local PCT-invariant interaction; with nonlocal interactions PCT violation and Lorentz invariance can coexist.
proof_status: Theorem 2 proved by the authors within perturbation theory.
relevance: Critic of Greenberg; lists the Wightman axioms that Jost's proof uses.
limits: Read whole in a text extraction.

title: Reversing the Arrow of Time
version: arXiv:2212.03489; Cambridge University Press 2022; chapter 8 DOI 10.1017/9781009122139.009 per the publisher's page as returned by search
locator: Sec. 2.5 (temporal orientation, Malament's proposal); Sec. 7.1; Sec. 7.4.1-7.4.2; Ch. 8 precis, Sec. 8.1 (Proposition 8.1), Sec. 8.2 (Segal quantisation argument, footnote 10)
assumptions: The author's Representation View: a spacetime symmetry has meaning in a dynamical theory through a representation.
conclusion: Author's claims: only the standard T is associated with an arrow of time itself; quantisation of classical time reversal does not exchange matter and antimatter; T violation requires a temporal orientation although it may not matter which.
open_questions: Whether matter-antimatter exchange is a spacetime symmetry in any sense (his Secs. 8.3-8.4, unread).
relevance: The main opposing view: T violation shows time itself has an asymmetry and CPT does not erase it. Also the concession that either orientation serves, and the quotations from Price, Greaves, Arntzenius and Greaves, and Wallace.
limits: Read through a text extraction of the arXiv copy: the passage on temporal orientation in Sec. 2.5, Sec. 7.1, Sec. 7.4 to the start of 7.4.3, and Chapter 8 from its opening to the end of Sec. 8.2. Secs. 8.3-8.4 and the rest of the book were not read. Quotations in RESULT.md are from Sec. 7.4.2.

title: On the time reversal invariance of classical electromagnetic theory
version: arXiv:gr-qc/0312085v1, 18 December 2003; Stud. Hist. Philos. Mod. Phys. 35 (2004) 295-315 as listed on the arXiv page
locator: Abstract; Sec. 1; Sec. 4 (action of time reversal on F and J, eq. (28), footnote 24); Sec. 7
assumptions: A temporally orientable relativistic spacetime; F and J determined relative to a temporal orientation; charge density as determined by an observer independent of the orientation.
conclusion: Author's claims: time reversal takes fields determined relative to one orientation to those determined relative to the other, giving -F and -J; Maxwell's equations are invariant; the equation with the gradient of F.F equal to J is not.
relevance: Time reversal as the flip of a temporal orientation, valid in curved spacetime; the example of a tensor equation that is not time reversal invariant.
limits: Read through a text extraction: abstract, Secs. 1-2, and the passages of Sec. 4 around eq. (28) and of Sec. 7. Secs. 3, 5 and 6 were not read in full.
